When evidence supports the narrative, it is celebrated.

When evidence contradicts the narrative, the person carrying the evidence gets attacked.

A jury heard the testimony. A jury examined the evidence. A jury found malpractice. And a jury put the damages at $2 million.

You protect them by listening.

posts.text:
Things my @bot setup does that still blow my mind:

1. A Chief of Staff who opens the day pulling open loops from email & tasks and suggesting things it can knock out before 7am.

2. After every meeting, decisions get folded into Notion, Linear, and Todoist — not left rotting in Granola

3. Every email starts as a draft. The CoS bot scans my email every ~2hr and drafts replies to nearly everything — including checking my cal for availability and finding requested attachments / links

4. A specialist for each lane: curriculum, engineering, coaching, hiring, content, ops, and one for every single piece of software

5. Routines that keep running while I’m offline (e.g. monitoring Sentry errors in our apps and proactively fixing things)

6. Group rooms where 2–4 bots share one project thread instead of me copy-pasting context

7. Cloud coding agents that pick up Linear issues and open PRs after running the list of open work by me EoD — then squash-merge to main when it’s done

8. Meeting prep briefs pulled from Granola + Notion before I walk in

9. A growing shareable knowledge base in Notion + a GitHub repo that we update daily based on what happens at school

10. Student progress look-up across Expertise, Followers, and CoFounder without inventing numbers — chat anytime to see where a student is on their business work

11. Mentor Mind that coaches me on how to hold the bar without inventing doctrine

12. Todoist as a central task list where it logs things it’s blocked on for me, or from meetings / emails — and I can paste links into chat to direct it how to solve them

13. Engineering work is automatically tracked in Linear so my and the product teams’ bots don’t collide with each other

14. Presentations spun up in Gamma / Claude Design without me opening a slide tool

15. Plaud / live capture → notes the bots can actually act on

Probably more but these were the immediate ones we thought of.

posts.text: Grok @Bot can be your personal chief financial officer!

quote.author: Teslaconomics
quote.name: Teslaconomics
quote.text:
I literally hooked up ALL my finance accounts to Grok Bot. 

I really mean all of them:

1/ Chase
2/ Charles Schwab
3/ E*TRADE
4/ Fidelity
5/ Robinhood
6/ Wealthfront
7/ Apple Card
8/ 𝕏 Money

FYI, this is a total of 30 accounts... Chase alone is 13 accounts between checking, savings, brokerage, credit cards, a 401(k), trusts, a stock plan, and 529s for the kids.

I was already honestly the best with my $ money and I’ve NEVER made a late payment in my life. But before Grok Bot, I was wasting so much time bc every answer lived in different apps. Like my cash was in one place, cards in another, brokerage accounts somewhere else, and had to compile everything in a spreadsheet, if I even got around to putting it together.

Now I just text my Grok Bot CFO.

I can ask, “What’s my cash right now?” and it pulls everything together and separates personal from business. I can ask which credit cards are coming due and whether I have enough cash to pay them all in full. Green means I’m covered, red means I’m short, and it tells me exactly how much I need. I actually tested this... going red on purpose. Like I moved $ money around so I would come up short on one of the upcoming bills, and Grok caught it.

I can even ask, “Where did my $ money go?” and instead of opening a bunch of apps, downloading transactions, cleaning up a spreadsheet, and making a chart myself, it pulls everything together and gives me the breakdown.

Today, I also asked it for a pie chart of all my stock investments with the amounts and percentages. 

1/ TSLA is 84.9%
2/ SPCX is 10.4%
3/ NVDA is 4.7% 

That’s across $ money sitting in different brokerage accounts, and it's awesome that I didn’t have to think about where any of it was. 

I literally just asked it one question... you can see for yourself. 

If you’re serious about your finances, you already ask the same questions all the time. 

• Like, can I cover everything that’s due? 
• Where did my $ money go? 
• How much $ cash do I really have? 
• What investments do I actually own? 

But honestly, the annoying part is that your financial life is usually scattered across 10+ different apps/platforms and a bunch of accounts, so getting a real answer takes a lot of work and your time. And honestly, most people probably don’t even look until something feels off or if they get a notification that a payment was missed or something.

Now, with all my finance accounts linked, I just ask a normal question, Grok Bot checks everything it has connected, and gives me the answer. Then I can ask the same thing tomorrow, and again whenever, and get the updated version without rebuilding anything.

The fact that you are able to talk to your entire financial life like you’re texting someone who already knows where everything is... this is a total game changer in the world of finance imo. 

If you really care about your $ money, hook yours up to Grok Bot. 

It's so worth it.

Jack Ma told Elon Musk humans will always be smarter than machines. 

Musk’s reaction says everything.

“Computers may be very clever, but human beings are much smarter. We invented the computer. I've never seen a computer invent a human being.”

Ma's argument was simple. Computers are tools. They calculate faster, remember more, but humans still hold something machines don't: experience, judgment, wisdom.

Musk clearly didn't buy it. “What would be an example of something that humans are better than a computer at?”

Watching this exchange now feels completely different than it did then. AI agents aren't just calculating anymore. They're writing code, analyzing documents, planning tasks, deciding what to do next on their own.

METR found that the length of software tasks frontier agents can complete autonomously has historically doubled roughly every seven months, with signs of even faster progress through parts of 2024.

That's where Ma's argument starts to buckle. For decades, technology automated what humans did. AI is starting to automate what we assumed required a human to think.

And companies were already learning to create enormous value with almost no people before this wave even arrived. Instagram sold for $1 billion with 13 employees. WhatsApp sold for $19 billion with 55.

Now picture what happens when a small team can direct hundreds of machines that never sleep, never take a salary, never need an office.

The question was never just which jobs disappear.

It's what happens to the money once fewer humans are needed to create it in the first place.

That's the question behind 2028: The Economy Without Humans.

Who gets the money when machines do the work?

The 10 billion at 15 years is an order of magnitude past that. 

Robots building robots still require saving, because energy, materials, and machines have to be bid into that line.
Expected abundance holds for ordinary wants which is what matters for people as consumers. Housing, food, care, and routine medicine get repriced toward energy and materials until a household’s budget stops being what limits them. 

An owner running 100s or 1,000s of agents earns the return on that capital stock, which is also how universal high income shows up as purchasing power. 

Money prices remain the way to allocate whatever is still scarce, that is energy, locations, raw materials. At least in the short term. 

Energy is the binding input, and settling more than one planet adds land, minerals, and generation beyond a single world.

TLDR: (1) More energy. (2) Multiplanetary doesn’t hurt.

Falcon 9 flew more missions in ONE YEAR than the entire Space Shuttle program flew in 30 years

• The entire Shuttle fleet:
135 missions from 1981–2011

• Falcon 9 in 2025 alone:
165 launches

SpaceX exceeded the Shuttle program’s entire lifetime mission count by 30 launches in just 12 months

And Falcon 9 also launched more times than every other orbital launch vehicle combined that year

At the Shuttle program’s historical average cadence, reaching 165 missions would have taken roughly 37 years

Falcon 9 did it in ONE

And the hardware reuse comparison is just as insane:

• Space Shuttle Discovery — 39 flights across roughly 27 years
• Falcon 9 booster B1067 — 37 flights in just over 5 years

B1067 first flew on June 3, 2021

By August 25, 2026, the same booster had launched and landed successfully 37 times

A single Falcon 9 first stage came within TWO flights of the most-flown Shuttle orbiter’s lifetime flight count in about one-fifth of the time

What once took decades of launch operations now happens within a single year of Falcon 9 cadence

SpaceX turned reusability into an industrial-scale operation

When Lauren Friedman showed up at Amherst College, she was surprised to discover that almost every single girl in her dorm and on her athletic team was already taking SSRIs.

Inside jokes about Zoloft & Lexapro were common on campus, and everyone seemed deeply grateful their persistent anxiety and depression from teenage years was magically disappearing from a pharmaceutical drug.

Like her peers, @lololizzle had struggled earlier in life with both anxiety and depression -- so Zoloft seemed like a perfect solution. After all, all of her friends were taking it too, so how bad could it be?

Little did she know, SSRIs are causing a silent epidemic among Gen Zers called Post-SSRI Sexual Dysfunction, or PSSD. Like untold tens of thousands of other people just like her, Lauren now has completely lost her libido, sensation in her genitals, and even a sense of emotional connection with the people around her... PERMANENTLY.

She says she and others like her were NEVER given informed consent about the risk of developing PSSD, and American doctors will rarely even diagnose the condition at all.

Whether it's birth control being thrown in the faces of teenage girls to magically "regulate your hormones" or Zoloft instantly prescribed to "make you happy," one thing is clear--the young women of Generation Z are being poisoned en masse without any understanding of what may happen to them down the line.
